newsitem.title: USA: Chile's Aninat sees inflation goals as viable.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Aninat sees inflation goals as viable.

text.p: Chile's Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said Monday that government projections of 6.5 percent inflation this year and 5.5 percent in 1997 were attainable if temporary elements are cleared from the data.

"If you clear the inflation CPI rate for transitory phenomena, you would see that the objective of 6.5 nominal inflation for this year, and 5.5 percent for next year is viable task," Aninat told reporters here.
The transitory phenomena included the hike in oil prices and the seasonal variables of foodstuffs, he said.
Aninat also said that sticking to inflation projections would require good coordination between monetary and fiscal policy.
The minister added that, when he presents the 1997 budget next week, he would emphasize the need for fiscal discipline.

"I will focus on the issue of fiscal savings, controlling the budget and looking at the revenue and expenditure sides of the equation, so as to produce convergence not only at the rate of growth level but at the absolute levels," he said.
